idiom_name: content: @Composable (State) -> Unit parameters on a composable that owns the behaviour
implementation_notes: Compose's slot APIs are the direct realization: a composable owns the state (remember/rememberSaveable or a hoisted state holder) and takes one or more content lambdas, so the call site supplies the markup and the framework re-runs the composition when the state changes; the Android documentation describes slot APIs as 'a pattern Compose introduces to bring in a layer of customization on top of composables' and notes that composables usually take a content lambda while slot APIs expose several for specific uses. What replaces the classic wrapper/prop-getter structure is the lambda parameter itself - there is no attribute bag to spread, because the consumer writes ordinary composables - and the behaviour stays testable by hoisting the state into a plain holder.
pitfalls: State created inside the content lambda instead of the behaviour composable is re-created on recomposition, so expanded/selected resets or duplicates - remember it in the owner or hoist it.
A content lambda that captures state by value closes over a stale snapshot; pass the state as a slot parameter instead.
Lambda identity changes on every recomposition can defeat skipping; mark slot content stable or provide keys where the compiler cannot prove stability.
Snapshot state read only during composition means a lambda stored in a long-lived effect keeps a snapshot rather than live state.

variants.name: Classic View system: a custom View owns behaviour and exposes the drawing hook
variants.idiom_name: View subclass owning state + invalidate()/requestLayout() after each transition
variants.implementation_notes: Before Compose the same split is hand-written: a View subclass owns the state and the interaction, exposes properties and events, and asks the framework to redraw; the documentation for custom views stresses exposing property getter/setter pairs and calling invalidate()/requestLayout() after any change that affects appearance or size, which is exactly the manual re-render contract Compose automates. The 'consumer supplies the markup' half appears as attributes plus an exposed drawing/content hook (child views, a delegate, or an adapter) - or the consumer subclasses the view. Keep this for existing Views codebases; new Android UI should use the Compose slot variant.
pitfalls: Forgetting invalidate()/requestLayout() after a state change leaves stale pixels or a stale size even though the behaviour is correct.
View state is lost on configuration change unless saved through onSaveInstanceState or a ViewModel.
Custom drawing or content must be announced to accessibility services (content descriptions, virtual views) or the headless behaviour becomes invisible to screen readers.
